articles.title: Michael Sheen toxic waste documentary 'the tip of the iceberg'
articles.summary: One scientist says there are thousands of sites across the UK that need investigating.
articles.body:
A former Monsanto worker who spent three years helping seal toxic waste underground said staff had "cheap" protective equipment and were not told what they were burying.

Stephen Constance worked at the chemical giant's Newport factory in the 1990s and came forward after the BBC documentary Buried with Michael Sheen highlighted Wales' toxic waste legacy.

But the 14 sites identified in the programme are just the tip of the iceberg and there are about 20,000 high-concern sites in the UK, said Dr David Megson, the scientist involved in the documentary.

Eastman Chemical Company, which is responsible for Monsanto's legacy production in the UK, did not respond when asked to comment.

Constance was one of dozens of people who contacted BBC Wales after coverage of Sheen's investigation into Monsanto and the dumping of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs).

Researcher and whistleblower Douglas Gowan spent 50 years trying to persuade authorities to investigate what he believed was widespread dumping of industrial chemicals.

These included PCBs, which he called "some of the worst contaminants known to man", and were widely used in the 20th Century, including for lipstick and white goods.

They were banned in the UK in the 1970s and have since been banned by 151 countries.

Constance, 61, said working for Monsanto was "absolutely dreadful".

Looking back, he said it was "quite evident that nobody was fully appraised of the potential hazard that they were exposed to".

The material was already buried when Constance arrived and it was his job to dig a 6m-deep trench around the outside of the mound before it was sealed using plastic membrane sheets and liquid clay.

While he believes this prevented airborne contamination, he is unsure if it would have stopped contamination into the Earth due to the high water table linked to the tides.

When asked if he felt safe, he said: "In terms of what we knew was there and what we were potentially exposed to, no."

Constance is in remission from cancer after having follicular lymphoma .

"I'm not suggesting in any way at all that it's linked, but the thought did cross my mind," he said.

In the documentary, journalists Dan Ashby and Lucy Taylor reveal a memo from Monsanto dated to 1972 which found that it knew PCBs were a danger to human health and was closing its site in the US as a result of legal action from a town.

However, it then increased its work at the plant in Newport.

"The government in the UK told the industry 'we're not going to put any restrictions on importing PCBs'," said Ashby.

"So they begin importing from around the world, hundreds of tonnes of PCBs."

Dr Megson, a reader in chemistry and environmental forensics at Manchester Metropolitan University, led the scientific data collection in the documentary.

He said: "The country is in a really dire place.

"Public pressure is the only thing that's going to make this action happen. This is our only chance, if I'm being brutally honest.

"What our data shows is those sites are leaking and those sites are a chemical cocktail. Whether it's the PCBs alone is up for debate.

"PCBs are suspected carcinogens, so we think they can cause cancer."

The data he found stunned him after having met people who had been worried about PCB levels near their family home for more than 30 years, saying he found levels that were "pretty much the highest I've ever seen in anything we've tested".

He added: "It's made me feel quite uncomfortable about some of those sites and what could have happened to all of those people's friends and loved ones.

"The polluter just keeps getting away with stuff left, right and centre."

These chemicals are hard to clear up, but not impossible.

Ralph Davies, who has been in the chemical remediation industry for about 35 years, said he proposed a way of cleaning up the acid tar lake in Llwyneinion near Ruabon in 2007, but never heard back from Wrexham council.

He said was "amazed" how close it was to people's homes when he visited nearly 20 years ago.

"People are still saying it does not meet the threshold for remediation, that both angers me and saddens me," he added.

"The fact it is still there, untouched, is mind blowing."

A report by an environmental engineering consultancy in 2006, seen by BBC Wales, shows that the acid tar lagoon - one of the sites in the documentary - was known to be contaminated as early as 1979.

Among the known contaminants dumped at the site is 93,100 tonnes of acid sludge from Burmah Castrol and barrels of unknown substances suspected to be from Monsanto, the report said.

Over the next 27 years, there were 18 investigations, two remediation proposals and five treatment trials but, as of 2026, the acid tar lagoon remains.

The report identified 105 possible ways contamination from the site could affect people, wildlife, property or water supplies.

This included three uncapped mine shafts beneath the lagoon that were suggested as potential pathways for contaminant movement.

In the 1980s, Clwyd County Council bought the site and legally agreed to protect the previous owner from any past, present or future claims, costs or liabilities arising from the "escape or nuisance of noxious wastes".

BP, which is responsible for Burmah Castrol, said it had no comment to make.

Emeritus professor Sue Jordan, a researcher at Swansea University, said further monitoring and investigation was needed.

After reading the BBC article about the documentary , she said she and her colleagues thought it was "an eye-opener" and it made them think "maybe there is something in this pollution".

She added that researchers still did not fully understand why some health outcomes, including congenital anomalies and stillbirths, appear higher in Wales than in parts of the UK, and believes further research is needed.

"I would very much like the minister to turn around and say Public Health Wales will look at this," she said.

"We don't want anything brushed under the carpet."

John Browne, a lawyer specialising in industrial disease claims at Slater and Gordon, said cases involving historical contamination were difficult to investigate - but not impossible.

"Time passing makes cases more difficult to prove," he said.

"Witnesses' memories fade and locating [eye]witnesses becomes increasingly challenging and difficult."

However, he said scientific, medical and forensic evidence could help establish what happened and whether exposure to hazardous substances contributed to illness.

The key question is not simply what the law was at the time, but what was known about the risks, he said, adding: "Communities affected by contamination deserve transparency and clear answers."

Public Health Wales said its Welsh cancer intelligence and surveillance unit had collected and analysed "every single case of cancer" since the 1970s.

It added: "Based on the evidence currently available, there is no indication that historical environmental pollution is responsible for an increased risk of cancer, or any other disease or illness, in these areas."

Natural Resources Wales said the Environment Agency, its predecessor, investigated the acid tar lake in 2006 and 2008 but tests concluded it did not meet the legal definition of contaminated land.

"Therefore, responsibility for the site returned and remains with Wrexham County Council as regulator."

Wrexham council said, since these investigations 20 years ago, ongoing monitoring had not identified any significant changes and there was no statutory requirement for remediation.

The Welsh government said addressing contaminated land was one of its key priorities.

"A survey of local authorities carried out by Natural Resources Wales in 2015 identified more than 9,000 potential sites requiring further investigation.

"While not all of these sites will pose a risk to human health or the environment, this figure demonstrates the scale of the issue facing regulators in Wales.

"We now intend to develop a Wales-wide strategy to progressively restore post-industrial land, so that communities are no longer exposed to potential risks."

The UK government referred the BBC to the Welsh government when asked to comment.

Buried with Michael Sheen is available on BBC iPlayer

articles.title: Muere Dolly Parton: la fabulosa vida de una de las estrellas más queridas en imágenes
articles.summary: La cantante estrella de la música country, que surgió de orígenes humildes, llegó a convertirse en una de las artistas más queridas del mundo.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton, la superestrella de la música country originaria de las Grandes Montañas Humeantes de Tennessee, pasó de unos orígenes humildes a convertirse en una de las artistas más queridas del mundo.

Esta admiración global se reflejó este martes en la cantidad de mensajes y muestras de cariño que se produjeron tras conocerse la noticia de su muerte, a los 80 años.

A lo largo de una carrera que abarcó más de 60 años, vendió más de 100 millones de discos, escribió más de 3.000 canciones y ganó 11 premios Grammy, incluido un reconocimiento a la trayectoria artística.

Siempre se describió a sí misma, ante todo, como compositora. "Es mi forma de expresarme. Es mi terapia", dijo en una ocasión.

Dolly Rebecca Parton creció en la pobreza en una cabaña de una sola habitación a orillas del río Little Pigeon, en las montañas Smoky de Tennessee, siendo la cuarta de 12 hijos.

De niña, actuó en la radio y la televisión locales, y grabó su primer sencillo a los 13 años.

Tras mudarse a Nashville al día siguiente de graduarse en la escuela secundaria del condado de Sevier, Dolly Parton consiguió su primer éxito en solitario con Dumb Blonde en 1966.

En 1967, la estrella de la música country Porter Wagoner invitó a Parton a unirse a The Porter Wagoner Show , dándole un papel fijo en su programa de televisión de distribución nacional, así como un lugar en su espectáculo teatral itinerante.

Su gran éxito llegó con el álbum Hello, I'm Dolly .

El 4 de enero de 1969 se convirtió en miembro del Grand Ole Opry , el programa radiofónico de música country más antiguo de Estados Unidos.

Parton lo describió como la "iglesia de mi corazón" y dijo que participar en él era un sueño de toda la vida.

En una memorable sesión de composición en 1973, Parton escribió dos de sus mayores éxitos: Jolene y I Will Always Love You .

Tras haber escrito miles de canciones a lo largo de su dilatada carrera, Parton afirmó que componer canciones era su mayor forma de autoexpresión.

Conocida por su imagen extravagante y deslumbrante, Dolly Parton combinó lentejuelas, ingenio y encanto para mantener una carrera que abarcó desde la música country hasta el pop comercial.

Fue cabeza de cartel en festivales y se convirtió en una estrella mundial con álbumes como Here You Come Again .

Parton también se hizo famosa por colaboraciones memorables, en particular con Kenny Rogers, cuyo dúo Islands in the Stream se convirtió en uno de los éxitos más representativos de la década de 1980.

Si bien Dolly Parton es más conocida por su extensa carrera musical, su trabajo como actriz también ha dejado una huella imborrable en el público cinematográfico.

El papel que lanzó a la fama a Parton en la pantalla grande llegó en la comedia de oficina de 1980 9 to 5 , donde compartió cartel con Jane Fonda, Lily Tomlin y Dabney Coleman.

Su interpretación de Doralee Rhodes combinó un gran sentido del humor con calidez, lo que ayudó a redefinir las expectativas sobre los artistas que dan el salto de la música al cine.

Posteriormente participó en películas como The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas , junto a Burt Reynolds, y Steel Magnolias ("Magnolias de acero").

Esta última cuenta con un reparto monumental que incluye a Julia Roberts y Sally Field junto a Shirley MacLaine, Olympia Dukakis y Daryl Hannah.

En estas interpretaciones, Parton demostró un equilibrio entre humor y profundidad emocional, a menudo dotando a las escenas de una presencia discreta y marcada.

En 1986, Dolly Parton inauguró Dollywood, un parque temático en Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, cerca de su lugar de nacimiento.

Se convirtió en una importante atracción turística, uno de los parques temáticos regionales más visitados de EE.UU..

El éxito del parque ayudó a financiar la fundación benéfica de Parton y su programa de alfabetización.

A través de su Biblioteca de la Imaginación, fundada en honor a su padre, que no sabía leer, Dolly Parton regaló más de 100 millones de libros a niños de todo el mundo.

Su propio libro, Coat of Many Colours , fue el libro número 100 millones que ese programa donó a la colección de la Biblioteca del Congreso de Estados Unidos.

Un ayuntamiento de Escocia anunció que dedicaría un día al año a Dolly Parton para conmemorar el impacto de su programa de fomento de la lectura.

Parton donó personalmente millones a la investigación médica y al socorro en casos de desastre.

Reunió a un elenco estelar de artistas para un teletón de tres horas con el fin de recaudar fondos.

En 2024, prometió US$2 millones para ayudar a los damnificados por el huracán Helene en el este de Tennessee y los Apalaches, combinando una donación personal con el apoyo equivalente de sus empresas y su fundación.

La actuación de Parton en el Festival de Glastonbury de 2014 se convirtió rápidamente en una de las actuaciones más emblemáticas en la sección de "Leyendas" de la historia del evento.

Con una de las mayores afluencias diurnas que ha tenido el festival, estimada en más de 180.000 personas, convirtió el escenario Pyramid en un coro multitudinario, con interpretaciones de Jolene , 9 to 5 y I Will Always Love You que provocaron escenas de participación casi unánime del público.

paragraphs: Dolly Parton, la superestrella de la música country originaria de las Grandes Montañas Humeantes de Tennessee, pasó de unos orígenes humildes a convertirse en una de las artistas más queridas del mundo.
Esta admiración global se reflejó este martes en la cantidad de mensajes y muestras de cariño que se produjeron tras conocerse la noticia de su muerte, a los 80 años.

A lo largo de una carrera que abarcó más de 60 años, vendió más de 100 millones de discos, escribió más de 3.000 canciones y ganó 11 premios Grammy, incluido un reconocimiento a la trayectoria artística.
Siempre se describió a sí misma, ante todo, como compositora. "Es mi forma de expresarme. Es mi terapia", dijo en una ocasión.
Dolly Rebecca Parton creció en la pobreza en una cabaña de una sola habitación a orillas del río Little Pigeon, en las montañas Smoky de Tennessee, siendo la cuarta de 12 hijos.
De niña, actuó en la radio y la televisión locales, y grabó su primer sencillo a los 13 años.
Tras mudarse a Nashville al día siguiente de graduarse en la escuela secundaria del condado de Sevier, Dolly Parton consiguió su primer éxito en solitario con Dumb Blonde en 1966.

En 1967, la estrella de la música country Porter Wagoner invitó a Parton a unirse a The Porter Wagoner Show , dándole un papel fijo en su programa de televisión de distribución nacional, así como un lugar en su espectáculo teatral itinerante.
Su gran éxito llegó con el álbum Hello, I'm Dolly .
El 4 de enero de 1969 se convirtió en miembro del Grand Ole Opry , el programa radiofónico de música country más antiguo de Estados Unidos.
Parton lo describió como la "iglesia de mi corazón" y dijo que participar en él era un sueño de toda la vida.
En una memorable sesión de composición en 1973, Parton escribió dos de sus mayores éxitos: Jolene y I Will Always Love You .
Tras haber escrito miles de canciones a lo largo de su dilatada carrera, Parton afirmó que componer canciones era su mayor forma de autoexpresión.
Conocida por su imagen extravagante y deslumbrante, Dolly Parton combinó lentejuelas, ingenio y encanto para mantener una carrera que abarcó desde la música country hasta el pop comercial.
Fue cabeza de cartel en festivales y se convirtió en una estrella mundial con álbumes como Here You Come Again .
Parton también se hizo famosa por colaboraciones memorables, en particular con Kenny Rogers, cuyo dúo Islands in the Stream se convirtió en uno de los éxitos más representativos de la década de 1980.

articles.title: Chinese teens are turning to mind-numbing drugs to 'run away from reality'
articles.summary: Students are seeking prescription drugs because they fear failure, a teen tells the BBC.
articles.body:
At 14, *Xiaomei, a high-performing student from a coastal province in China, decided to overdose on cough medication.

She wanted to impress an older boy who told her it would help her relax. The tablets were usually only available with a doctor's prescription, but she managed to buy them online.

At first she found that they made her a bit dizzy. But she was soon hooked to the slightly numb sensation, which, to her, felt like a brief respite from the pressure of looming exams. When taken in large doses, the drug can cause serious side effects, including hallucinations and impaired coordination.

Eventually she tried other medication recommended to her on chat groups. Some were for pain or epileptic seizures. Sometimes she would take five tablets. Other times she would try more than 10 to feel the effects of different drugs.

For two years, she took large quantities of various prescription drugs. None of them were prescribed to her or anyone in her family. She bought them all on the internet.

"When I felt too much pressure from my studies, or I didn't do well at exams, or even when I quarrelled with my parents, I would take these drugs," she told the BBC. "I was running away from reality."

The BBC has heard similar stories from dozens of Chinese teenagers in chat rooms across various social media platforms. Nearly every one of them seemed to be escaping the same thing: pressure. They were doing that by chasing what is being described as a "pharmaceutical high".

One girl shared a voice note after taking large doses of a neuropathic pain drug. Her words were slurred and hard to comprehend: "I feel my body doesn't belong to me. I'm so dizzy."

"Just sleep," comes the advice. "You will be fine tomorrow."

One boy offered to use his father's old prescription to fake a new one for the same drug.

Some offered tips: "If you want to hallucinate, you can just buy... it's not been controlled yet," says one user, suggesting a drug used by people with Parkinson's to control tremors. In excessive doses it can cause confusion or even delirium.

"Which keyword should I use to search for it on online platforms," another user asks.

It is hard to gauge the scale of the problem, as there are few official figures.

But it is serious enough that the government launched a nationwide crackdown two years ago against the cough suppressant Xiaomei started using, classifying it as a psychotropic drug which would only be available to patients with a doctor's prescription. That made it much harder for young people to buy online.

Then in April this year, authorities noticed that young people had switched to another drug and imposed tighter controls on how it is prescribed and dispensed at chemists. Still the BBC was offered the drug in an online chat room for as little as 10 Chinese yuan ($1.5; £1.09) per gram.

"Non-regulated substances are easy to acquire and even when one drug is controlled by the authorities, young people quickly find alternatives," says a 2025 paper written for the Crime Prevention Institute at the Ministry of Justice.

In some cases the BBC found that teens online were using different names for drugs to avoid detection, which the 2025 study also noted.

There is growing evidence that young people across the world are turning to prescription medication to fight off pressures and anxiety .

So easy access to cheap prescription drugs in China is perhaps not that surprising given that it produces the vast majority of the world's pharmaceutical ingredients.

When Xiaomei wanted to buy the cough suppressant, it just took a few clicks for an entire box of the medication to be delivered at her door, she says. "You could simply enter your ID number on shopping platforms and buy it directly."

The ID, which is a national identity number, includes her age but she says she was still sold the drug, no questions asked. It was also cheap - often 50 tablets cost less than a dollar.

On paper, China is winning the war on illegal drugs. Official data for 2025 shows a dramatic fall - 41% - in newly identified drug users under the age of 35.

However authorities have had to acknowledge that the misuse of prescription drugs is becoming a widespread problem. It has been especially surging among minors, China's National Narcotics Control Commission warned in a recent report.

Xiaomei says that a lot of students in her elite chemistry class were discussing ways to overdose on prescription drugs to avoid feeling like "complete losers".

"It is just so hard to pass exams and to stay in elite classes. In our school, the elite classes operate on an elimination system; if your academic scores drop, you get kicked out of the class. When you fail, you feel like failures, believing you have no chance in life."

Part of the pressure comes from parents who also see their child as their only hope for the future, says renowned Chinese sociologist and director of the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology, Xiang Biao.

Because of the one-child policy which ended in 2016 after decades, many families only have one child, Biao adds, who shoulders all their expectations.

"What makes Chinese teens different is their isolating environment. They spend at least nine or 10 hours in school. They have very few chances to develop social relationships, very few opportunities to witness what life is really like."

More worrying, he sees a link between prescription drug abuse and an increase in self-harm. The BBC noticed, for instance, that in many of the chat rooms, young people would encourage one another to cut themselves "to feel something".

As an extremely competitive high school entrance exam drew close, Xiaomei tried a different drug, searching for ways to numb the anxiety.

"But my memory deteriorated rapidly," she says. "I couldn't remember anything clearly, and I lived in a constant daze."

The drug is usually prescribed to help control epileptic seizures and it works as neuropathic pain medication. When Xiaomei explained the side effects in one of her chat groups, they suggested another drug, which is given as pain relief. She says it gave her some release but she soon needed higher doses.

Months before sitting the important exam, she went too far.

She'd taken 50 tablets and started to panic. "I was afraid something serious might happen, but I didn't want to have my stomach pumped so I wanted to wait before telling my parents."

But she became so unwell that she had to confess.

Her parents decided to listen to what they saw as their daughter's cry for help.

"They mostly expressed how heartbreaking it was for them to see me like that. They didn't scold or criticise me. Their approach was gentle."

For her, this has made all the difference.

"Many children receive lots of attention but the type of attention they want is to be asked how they feel. Do they feel lonely or stressed? Often in China parents brush that away and say you just have to be stronger," Biao says.

"There's a very loud alarm being sounded out across Chinese society. Adults have to examine how to be responsible for a teenager. Having an open conversation as a family - that is probably the most rewarding part of life."

And that is where the real battle lies, according to experts. Rather than playing whack-a-mole trying to suppress online sales of prescription drugs, the government should focus on what may well be a mental health crisis, they say.

In 2023, a study for China's Mental Health Blue Book found that nearly 95 million people suffer from depression and more than 30% were under 18 years old.

The Chinese government has recognised the need for mental health support for teens. Those plans include counselling rooms in every school, psychiatric services in at least one hospital in every county and more mental health professionals. The aim is to build a nationwide system of psychological support and crisis intervention by 2030.

So far they have been quite successful. According to the State Council, 92% of primary schools and 95% of junior middle schools now have a counsellor. Many major cities, including Beijing, have started to incorporate mental health into the curriculum.

However, there is still a major shortage of medical psychiatrists specialising in children and adolescents.

A 2020 study published in British medical journal The Lancet claimed there were only 500 qualified child psychiatrists in the country, and many of them were based in major cities such as Beijing and Shanghai.

This is a huge challenge in a country that has undergone three decades of unprecedented social and economic change.

The China Xiaomei's parents grew up in is very different from the future she is facing. Her parents followed a script set by the Communist Party: work hard and you will be rewarded. Now, even if young adults pass with high grades and get a university degree, a bright future is not guaranteed.

Following gruelling pandemic restrictions, the Chinese economy has struggled to bounce back. One in five young people are thought to be struggling to find a job and families are spending less.

"People have become more pessimistic in general," Biao admits. And the anxiety extends to adults, he adds.

"I think parents feel confused and anxious because they see a problem in their children, but they don't see an alternative. If my child has a problem, it's the end of the world. If my child doesn't do well in school, it's the end of the world. If my child doesn't speak to me, it's the end of the world. I think we should pay more attention to parents as well as children."

Fortunately Xiaomei and her parents have managed to find a way to cross this bridge.

"In the past, my parents didn't really understand me and would say some pretty harsh things. I felt like I had no help and was truly on my own," she says.

But that changed when she was rushed to hospital after the overdose. They started listening to her and talking to her, and "knowing that there was someone standing by my side made me feel really good", she says. It even helped her perform well in the entrance exam she had been dreading for so long.

"I am lucky to have their support," she adds.

Not everyone finds such support though, and that's where *Lu Jingchan hopes he can help.

The 22-year-old spent years battling depression. He found it hard to beat the euphoria that came from taking prescription drugs, and overdosed more than four times in four years.

"The drugs drove me to the brink of madness. You risk sinking into an abyss of addiction, destroying your health," he says.

He has now quit all prescription medication, and spends his time on social media urging others not to start. And he has this advice for young people battling the pressures he once did.

"I hope you can face life head-on, without needing medicines to numb yourselves. If you are overdosing, I want to give you the courage to stop. I believe your lives will improve. I believe you will all find happiness."

* Names have been changed to protect their identity

"There's a very loud alarm being sounded out across Chinese society. Adults have to examine how to be responsible for a teenager. Having an open conversation as a family - that is probably the most rewarding part of life."

And that is where the real battle lies, according to experts. Rather than playing whack-a-mole trying to suppress online sales of prescription drugs, the government should focus on what may well be a mental health crisis, they say.
In 2023, a study for China's Mental Health Blue Book found that nearly 95 million people suffer from depression and more than 30% were under 18 years old.

The Chinese government has recognised the need for mental health support for teens. Those plans include counselling rooms in every school, psychiatric services in at least one hospital in every county and more mental health professionals. The aim is to build a nationwide system of psychological support and crisis intervention by 2030.

So far they have been quite successful. According to the State Council, 92% of primary schools and 95% of junior middle schools now have a counsellor. Many major cities, including Beijing, have started to incorporate mental health into the curriculum.
However, there is still a major shortage of medical psychiatrists specialising in children and adolescents.

A 2020 study published in British medical journal The Lancet claimed there were only 500 qualified child psychiatrists in the country, and many of them were based in major cities such as Beijing and Shanghai.
This is a huge challenge in a country that has undergone three decades of unprecedented social and economic change.

The China Xiaomei's parents grew up in is very different from the future she is facing. Her parents followed a script set by the Communist Party: work hard and you will be rewarded. Now, even if young adults pass with high grades and get a university degree, a bright future is not guaranteed.
Following gruelling pandemic restrictions, the Chinese economy has struggled to bounce back. One in five young people are thought to be struggling to find a job and families are spending less.
"People have become more pessimistic in general," Biao admits. And the anxiety extends to adults, he adds.

"I think parents feel confused and anxious because they see a problem in their children, but they don't see an alternative. If my child has a problem, it's the end of the world. If my child doesn't do well in school, it's the end of the world. If my child doesn't speak to me, it's the end of the world. I think we should pay more attention to parents as well as children."
Fortunately Xiaomei and her parents have managed to find a way to cross this bridge.
"In the past, my parents didn't really understand me and would say some pretty harsh things. I felt like I had no help and was truly on my own," she says.

But that changed when she was rushed to hospital after the overdose. They started listening to her and talking to her, and "knowing that there was someone standing by my side made me feel really good", she says. It even helped her perform well in the entrance exam she had been dreading for so long.
"I am lucky to have their support," she adds.
Not everyone finds such support though, and that's where *Lu Jingchan hopes he can help.
The 22-year-old spent years battling depression. He found it hard to beat the euphoria that came from taking prescription drugs, and overdosed more than four times in four years.
"The drugs drove me to the brink of madness. You risk sinking into an abyss of addiction, destroying your health," he says.
He has now quit all prescription medication, and spends his time on social media urging others not to start. And he has this advice for young people battling the pressures he once did.

"I hope you can face life head-on, without needing medicines to numb yourselves. If you are overdosing, I want to give you the courage to stop. I believe your lives will improve. I believe you will all find happiness."
* Names have been changed to protect their identity

articles.title: Klay Thompson points to 'redemption season' in Miami
articles.summary: "The opportunity to win again at a very high level was so attractive to me."
articles.body:
One doesn't have to look too hard on social media to find someone using the word "washed" in the same sentence as Klay Thompson 's name.

Which is exactly why the four-time champion and future Hall of Famer wanted to join the Heat , Thompson said at his introductory press conference, via the Associated Press .

"It's kind of a redemption season for me to show I can still make an impact on winning and do it consistently," Thompson said. "I can't wait to get to work. It's pretty surreal being here. But what an honor it is....

"I've tasted winning before and there's really nothing like it. The opportunity to win again at a very high level was so attractive to me."

Thompson put his money where his mouth was about winning, giving up more than $9 million of his $17.5 million contract to facilitate a buyout in Dallas . Then he signed with the Heat for two years, $11.5 million (more total money, less per year), making about $5.6 million this season (low enough that the Heat can fill out their roster with two veteran minimum contracts).

Thompson got into more detail about what he wants sitting down with Brendan Tobin .

"I just missed out on the postseason [last season with the Warriors ]. I hate watching from home. You get FOMO watching all your coworkers just getting to chase their dreams and it's not fun not making the playoffs. That's all I want to do these next couple years. Have a chance to make a deep postseason run. So excited to be in Miami . They're a very demanding organization, but I love being in that ultra-competitive atmosphere, and this was a match made in heaven."

Thompson should get his chance to compete in the postseason this season. He is expected to start in Miami, a team that has worked to put as much shooting as possible around Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo . Last season, Thompson averaged a career-low 11.7 points a game but shot 38.3% from 3-point range on a healthy 7.6 attempts per game — he should thrive in the up-tempo offense expected from the Heat. Expect him to hit a lot of trail and corner 3-pointers in transition.

The opportunities will be there for Thompson to prove all his detractors wrong, to get his redemption. He just has to grab them.

articles.title: U.S. military says it killed four in strike on alleged drug-smuggling boat in the Caribbean
articles.summary: The latest attack brings the number of people who have been killed in boat strikes by the U.S. military to at least 227 in 68 strikes since the Trump administration began targeting those it calls “narcoterrorists” almost a year ago.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — The U.S. military attacked a boat suspected of being used to smuggle drugs in the Caribbean Sea on Tuesday, killing four people, as the Trump administration continues its monthslong campaign against alleged traffickers in Latin America. The latest attack brings the number of people who have been killed in boat strikes by the U.S. military to at least 227 in 68 strikes since the Trump administration began targeting those it calls “narcoterrorists” almost a year ago. As with most of the military’s statements on strikes in the eastern Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea, U.S. Southern Command said it targeted the alleged drug traffickers along known smuggling routes. The military did not provide evidence that the vessel was ferrying drugs. A video posted on X showed an image of what appeared to be a moving boat followed by a flash. Tuesday’s strike came just two days after the U.S. military carried out a strike on a vessel in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing two people accused of trafficking drugs. That action came after a pause of more than two months in the U.S. campaign against alleged smugglers. The Trump administration is pursuing deals with allied nations to extend its offensive to land across multiple Latin American countries. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said during a visit to Panama this month that Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras had agreed to allow the U.S. to carry out joint military operations against criminal groups on their soil. Guatemala denied reaching such a deal. Ecuador launched similar missions with the U.S. in March. President Donald Trump has said the U.S. is in “armed conflict” with cartels in Latin America and has justified the attacks as a necessary escalation to stem the flow of drugs into the United States and fatal overdoses claiming American lives. But his administration has offered little evidence to support its claims of killing smugglers.

articles.title: Yordan Alvarez hits go-ahead triple in 8th inning as Astros outlast Yankees 9-7
articles.summary: Yordan Alvarez went 3 for 5 and lined a go-ahead triple in the eighth inning off Brent Headrick as the Houston Astros beat the New York Yankees 9-7 on Tuesda...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Yordan Alvarez went 3 for 5 and lined a go-ahead triple in the eighth inning off Brent Headrick as the Houston Astros beat the New York Yankees 9-7 on Tuesday night.

Yainer Diaz hit a pair of solo homers, including a tying shot to the short porch in right field off Headrick's fastball to start the eighth. After Jeremy Pena singled, Alvarez ripped a low-inside sinker to the warning track in right-center for a 7-6 lead.

Alvarez increased his major league-leading batting average to .323. The slugger had his seventh career triple and first since July 21, 2024.

Pena homered off Fernando Cruz in the sixth for a 5-all tie. Daulton Varsho had two RBI singles for the Astros, who won for the sixth time in 15 games after owner Jim Crane said manager Joe Espada will finish the season.

Isaac Paredes added an RBI single off Headrick (7-3), who has allowed five homers in 68 appearances. Headrick is second in the big leagues in appearances to Toronto lefty Mason Fluharty and permitted a run for only the 12th time.

Diaz tacked on an RBI single in the ninth off rookie Bradley Hanner as the Astros scored six runs against New York's bullpen.

Houston overcame a four-hit night by New York first baseman Luis García Jr. García hit an RBI double off Steven Okert that gave the Yankees a 6-5 lead and also launched a two-run homer in the fifth off rookie starter Ethan Packo.

It was García's third four-hit game this season and the eighth of his career.

Bryan Abreu (5-3) allowed an RBI single to Jazz Chisholm Jr. before finishing a double play against Austin Wells with a nice grab at first base. Josh Hader got four outs for his 19th save in 19 chances.

Cody Bellinger hit a three-run homer in the third that broke a 32-game homerless drought and gave the Yankees a 3-2 lead.

Packo allowed five runs and five hits in 4 1/3 innings on his 24th birthday.

New York starter Will Warren permitted three runs — two earned — and seven hits in five innings.

Astros RHP Peter Lambert (8-7, 3.68 ERA) pitches Wednesday night. The Yankees had not announced a scheduled starter.

articles.title: ‘People can think what they want': Wyndham Clark responds to rules ‘scrutiny'
articles.summary: Wyndham Clark, at the Tour Championship, responds to rules "scrutiny" after a move at the BMW Championship.
articles.body:
Wyndham Clark says he didn't take "a bad lie and make it good."

And if you think that he did during Sunday's final round of the BMW Championship?

"People can think what they want," Clark said.

His comments came Tuesday ahead of this week's Tour Championship , where he was asked about a scene to the right of the 14th hole at Bellerive Country Club, host of the BMW. There, while Clark prepared to hit his second shot on the par-4, a CBS camera positioned to his right caught the following:

– Clark grabbed an iron from his bag, placed it behind his ball, then took a practice swing just to the left of the ball. Twice more, he placed his iron behind the ball and took practice swings, before going back to his bag for a different iron. At the time, Clark was tied for the lead with Rory McIlroy.

– CBS cut away to Gary Woodland on the 15th hole.

– When it returned, Clark was placing an iron behind his ball. He then took another practice swing to the left of it before his caddie, David Pelekoudas, moved between Clark and the camera, though another practice swing could be seen. Clark then went back to his bag for a different iron. Three times, he placed that iron behind his ball and took practice swings. At about this point, CBS analysts said the following:

Trevor Immelman: "He's taking a long look at this. This is like the third club that he's placed down behind the ball there."

Frank Nobilo: "So the lie might be better."

From there, Clark placed his 9-iron behind the ball and hit, finished the hole with a par and went on to win by three . But Nobilo's comment, along with several similar remarks on social media, is interesting. Did Clark improve his lie? On Tuesday, Clark was asked the following question:

Wyndham, your drive on 14 Sunday went into the right rough, and there was a lot of scrutiny on social media but also even the TV announcers. Curious about you changing clubs and tapping down the rough multiple times. Just curious what you were thinking there, and there was a similar situation possibly at the U.S. Open, and if you've been hearing about this at all.

"I didn't really hear much about it," Clark said. "I know the shot that you're talking about. I think any player, when they're trying to judge a lie, takes out different clubs to see what it feels like.

"I never fully put the club down behind it. I don't think anything of it."

Match play included in PGA Tour's radically new postseason structure

As part of his answer, he also noted a pair of previous incidents in which his actions around the ball have been questioned — during the third round of the 2024 Arnold Palmer Invitational , Clark placed his iron behind his ball, causing the grass and ball to move, though no rules penalty was assessed; then, at this year's U.S. Open , a video of Clark stepping on the grass around his ball circulated online. On Tuesday, Clark also brought up the actions of Bryson DeChambeau at this year's Open Championship, where DeChambeau was penalized for improving the area around his intended swing.

"When the cameras are on you, they're going to find anything," Clark said. "And I think you saw that in Bryson's case. It happened to me at the U.S. Open, it happened to me at Bay Hill. It's happened to a lot of guys where they can see stuff that maybe looks like something that maybe it's not."

Rule 8.1b (4) states that players are allowed to, "ground the club lightly right in front of or right behind the ball," with "ground the club lightly" meaning, "allowing the weight of the club to be supported by the grass, soil, sand or other material on or above the ground surface."

"That lie was never bad," Clark said Tuesday. "It was more just judging what it was. By no means did I take a bad lie and make it really good.

"People can think what they want. I know I didn't do anything that was costing the integrity of the field. That's all I've got to say about that."

The post 'People can think what they want': Wyndham Clark responds to rules 'scrutiny' appeared first on Golf .

articles.title: Alabama OC Ryan Grubb provides update on offensive line
articles.summary: Alabama's offensive line still has a few question marks as fall camp nears its conclusion. The Tide rotated through several players up front in 2025, specifi...
articles.body:
TUSCALOOSA, Ala. ( WIAT ) — Alabama's offensive line still has a few question marks as fall camp nears its conclusion. The Tide rotated through several players up front in 2025, specifically at left guard.

According to offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb, the offensive line's five starters are almost set.

"I think we're close," Grubb said. "We're right to game week, and it's been pretty consistently the same five."

He singled out the left guard battle as one that will come down to sophomore Mal Waldrep and junior Will Sanders.

"There's still a couple battles that are lingering. Specifically, Mal and Will have been trading off one reps," Grubb said. "Other than that, it's been pretty consistent."

Alabama opens its season at home against East Carolina on Sept. 5.

articles.title: From ‘ridiculous’ to a viral success: Akron’s offensive coordinator contest has been a big hit
articles.summary: Some people thought Andrew Goodrich was bonkers when he suggested that the University of Akron hold a contest to name an “Offensive Coordinator of the Game”...
articles.body:
AKRON, Ohio (AP) — Some people thought Andrew Goodrich was bonkers when he suggested that the University of Akron hold a contest to name an "Offensive Coordinator of the Game" for its home opener against Robert Morris on Sept. 12.

But after the Zips' athletic director explained and refined the idea, the promotion has turned out to be a public relations success and a revenue driver.

Akron garnered 23 million social media views and an influx of new season ticket-holders since the contest was announced Aug. 4.

"I just wanted to do something that no one had ever done before. And maybe more importantly than that, I wanted to do something that would make fans read that and look at their friend and go, 'Are you serious? Would I really have a chance to do this?' And that's what we were looking for," Goodrich said. "We thought it would be popular in our backyard of maybe the MAC, northeast Ohio and western Pennsylvania. We didn't realize that the whole world was going to go, 'Hey, you know what? We love this.'"

Marty Whims II, a longtime season ticket-holder, was announced as the winner Tuesday. Whims graduated from Akron and is the chief financial officer for Stark Enterprises.

Akron's College of Business and the George W. Daverio School of Accountancy conducted the random drawing.

"It's a unique opportunity. The football program benefits from season tickets and then shines us in a positive light. I never had on my bingo card that I'd be on TMZ Sports," coach Joe Moorhead said. "Like I told our players when they heard about it, I said, 'I'm not going to let the circus roll into town. It ain't happening under my watch.' It's going to give somebody a unique opportunity, but I'm never going to make a mockery of the game or disrespect our opponent."

Whims will get to call one series. Moorhead's sheet for the opening series includes 12 to 24 plays.

The idea was formed during a plane trip back from March Madness

Goodrich first had the idea on a flight from Tampa, Florida, after the Zips were eliminated by Texas Tech in the first round of the NCAA men's basketball tournament on March 20.

Senior deputy AD and chief operating officer Matt Pottorff told Goodrich it was a terrible idea when he first heard it, until they discussed it more.

Letting a fan be an OC for an entire game was a nonstarter and calling one play wasn't enough of a selling point. Calling one series, though, was a happy medium.

Pottorff said the two biggest issues that remained were getting buy-in from Coach Moorhead and announcing it when it would get more attention.

"We wanted to be just basically at the right time with ticket sales and ticket staff," Pottorff said. "We had kind of all hands on deck at this point to make sure everybody's ready. But we didn't think that this was going to be anywhere near as huge as it ended up being."

Moorhead, who is his own offensive coordinator, was initially skeptical.

"At first I thought it was absolutely ridiculous. I don't even let my assistant coaches call plays. I call the plays," he said. "As we talked through it a little bit more and discussed some of the guardrails and parameters where, 'Hey, this guy's not bringing in a single-wing playbook and putting it in Friday before the game.' He's going to come in, you'll walk them through what's in the game plan. You'll talk about, 'Hey, this is what Robert Morris plays in all these different situations. Here's my opening script for the game. What are your ideas? And then, hey, what do you think about this play in this position?' And make it more of a collaboration, for lack of a better term."

Only those with season tickets or suites were eligible for the contest. Besides new season-ticket sales, suites sold out for the first time since InfoCision Stadium opened in 2009. Jon Gruden, Pat McAfee and Dan "Big Cat" Katz ended up ponying up for season tickets, as well as fans from 38 states and as far away as Germany.

Every season and suite ticket counted as an entry (four tickets, four entries). Season ticket-holders also received additional entries for each new season ticket buyer they referred.

The nine finalists were announced Aug. 19, including Katz of Barstool Sports, longtime season ticket-holders, and people from Nebraska and Texas.

The promotion even got a last-minute corporate sponsor with fast-food chain Arby's coming aboard.
paragraphs: AKRON, Ohio (AP) — Some people thought Andrew Goodrich was bonkers when he suggested that the University of Akron hold a contest to name an "Offensive Coordinator of the Game" for its home opener against Robert Morris on Sept. 12.
But after the Zips' athletic director explained and refined the idea, the promotion has turned out to be a public relations success and a revenue driver.
Akron garnered 23 million social media views and an influx of new season ticket-holders since the contest was announced Aug. 4.

"I just wanted to do something that no one had ever done before. And maybe more importantly than that, I wanted to do something that would make fans read that and look at their friend and go, 'Are you serious? Would I really have a chance to do this?' And that's what we were looking for," Goodrich said. "We thought it would be popular in our backyard of maybe the MAC, northeast Ohio and western Pennsylvania. We didn't realize that the whole world was going to go, 'Hey, you know what? We love this.'"
Marty Whims II, a longtime season ticket-holder, was announced as the winner Tuesday. Whims graduated from Akron and is the chief financial officer for Stark Enterprises.
Akron's College of Business and the George W. Daverio School of Accountancy conducted the random drawing.

"It's a unique opportunity. The football program benefits from season tickets and then shines us in a positive light. I never had on my bingo card that I'd be on TMZ Sports," coach Joe Moorhead said. "Like I told our players when they heard about it, I said, 'I'm not going to let the circus roll into town. It ain't happening under my watch.' Whims will get to call one series. Moorhead's sheet for the opening series includes 12 to 24 plays.

articles.summary: Observations from Lincoln Financial Field.
articles.body:
Tonight marked the sixteenth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Here's what I observed from the team's one and only public session of the summer at Lincoln Financial Field!

EAGLES INJURY REPORT: IN-PRACTICE INJURIES: OT Lane Johnson seemed to get banged up early in practice. He went to the sideline and talked to a trainer. He remained on the sideline for the rest of practice with a helmet in his hand. He did seem to be shaking his left leg around at times. Fred Johnson filled in for Lane at right tackle (no practice for Markel Bell). DT Jordan Davis suffered an upper body injury and was looked at by trainers. He put a brace on his arm and returned to team drills. TE E.J. Jenkins suffered an upper body injury and was looked at by trainers. DID NOT PARTICIPATE: OG Landon Dickerson (not injury related/rest) It's worth noting that Dickerson was carted off the field with an injury at last year's public practice . TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) OT Markel Bell (thumb/leg) CB Jonathan Jones (shoulder) CB Jakorian Bennett (knee) TE Grant Calcaterra (back) S Cole Wisniewski (concussion) LIMITED PARTICIPATION: CB Mac McWilliams (shoulder) REMOVED FROM THE INJURY REPORT: OG Willie Lampkin Lampkin got banged up on Saturday night and missed Monday's practice. RB Dameon Pierce Pierce missed a lot of camp before recently returning to practice in a limited capacity. Now he's full go. DT Byron Young Young was limited on Monday. OT John Ojukwu Ojukwu was limited on Monday. WR Danny Gray Gray was limited on Monday. DT Gabe Hall Hall wasn't actually on the injury report but he did appear to get banged up on Monday. Apparently he's OK.

Hurts hit Darius Cooper on a curl for first down yardage. Hurts threw a nice ball to Saquon Barkley , who made an over-the-shoulder touchdown grab with Zack Baun trailing (see video below).

JALEN HURTS UPDATE (continued): THE BAD: As I've previously noted, Hurts has thrown a lot of interceptions this summer. Certainly much more than he has in previous training camps ( Eliot Shorr-Parks' charting says 13 INTs … after having 15 in the last four training camps combined ). Is this the end of the world? No. Well, I'm sure the ever-so turnover-averse Nick "End every drive with a kick" Sirianni doesn't love it. And it's obviously not ideal. But I don't think it would be accurate to say he's had a bad summer just because he's thrown a lot of picks. After watching the offense go overboard on turnover avoidance at all costs last season, I think it's good to see Hurts taking some more chances. The offense has had good moments, just as there were some tonight. But there's obviously a balance to be struck between being aggressive and being reckless. I don't think Hurts has been the latter. But we'll see if this trend carries over into the regular season or not. Hurts threw a pass to Lemon on a slant that was knocked down by Quinyon Mitchell . A Hurts deep shot to DeVonta Smith was a bit underthrown. DeVonta still had a chance to make the play, which he didn't … in part because Mitchell was able to make up ground while DeVonta slowed down. Let's talk Riq Woolen! Well, we've already mentioned him. But just wanted to stress that he had a strong night with the two picks. As we said last week, it's not always going to be pretty with him. He will be frustrating at times. But while there might be some low lows, there will also be pretty high highs. He's a playmaker and a net positive.

Kinda feel like Nolan Smith is being slept on. He beat Lane Johnson (!) to the inside to notch a "sack" on Hurts early in practice. Not sure if this was the rep where Lane got banged up. Smith's been overshadowed by Jalyx Hunt 's ascent to potential stardom but he's no chopped liver.

Speaking of Jalyx, he was cooking Fred Johnson tonight. There was a rep where he beat Big Fred around the edge for what probably would've been a strip-sack by getting to Hurts in his windup. Hunt also had a nice rep in coverage where he was in position to blow up DeVonta Smith in the flat after a short reception from under center play-action.

Jalen Carter had an excellent swim move to beat a blocker (think it was either Cam Jurgens or Tyler Steen ) and be in position for a TFL on Saquon Barkley.

Drew Kendall logged first-team left guard reps tonight with Dickerson resting.

Tank Bigsby had a couple nice runs that looked like they would've went for big gains.

BACKUP QUARTERBACK BATTLE UPDATE: Andy Dalton was first up at QB2 tonight. He overthrew Darius Cooper to the left side, not unlike how the veteran previously missed Cooper and Eli Stowers on Saturday night. Dalton did later hit a crossing Elijah Moore , who was schemed wide open, for a catch-and-run touchdown. Tanner McKee threw a good ball to Hollywood Brown along the right sideline at one point. He also made another connection with Darius Cooper to move the offense into plus territory during a two-minute drill towards the end of practice. McKee also found Moore to get into field goal range before the drive ultimately stalled just outside of the red zone.

Darius Cooper had a couple nice catches tonight. He also had a bad drop and there was a rep where it didn't look like he was on the same page as McKee. Even so, I'd argue that Cooper is more ready to contribute early in the season than Lemon is. Obviously, the Eagles' 2026 first-round pick is making his way back from injury. It's possible that Lemon will look more ready by the time Week 1 is here. Or maybe he won't but the Eagles playing him to work out the kinks will pay off later in the season. But if the Eagles had to play a game today, Cooper is one of the Eagles' best three receivers at this moment in time.

The Eagles' defense was all over designed touches to Lemon. Hurts and Lemon have also yet to totally sync up.

Lemon is in the running to be the Eagles' punt returner. He took reps in that role along with Britain Covey and Cooper DeJean .

Jose Ramirez doesn't have a chance to make the roster, in part because the Eagles are really deep at edge rusher. But he's popped in practice and the preseason games. Would be a good guy to get on the practice squad. He was pretty dominant in his final year at Eastern Michigan, when he logged 19.5 TFLs and 12 sacks in 12 games played. Ramirez showed up with a TFL tonight.

With Lane Johnson getting banged up, Markel Bell not practicing, and Fred Johnson filling in at right tackle, John Ojukwu saw some first-team left tackle action with Jordan Mailata getting some reps off.

No fight this time around but Moro Ojomo drove Fred Johnson multiple yards into the backfield on a rep where Barkley was stopped for just a short gain to bring up a fourth down.

For those wondering why the players were wearing jerseys with bright green numbers, it's to promote the Eagles Autism Foundation . They'll be auctioned off for charity if you want to get your hands on one.

Today I learned that former Eagles long snapper Jon Dorenbos has really long hair now.

Jolene by Dolly Parton was played on the speakers at The Linc after tonight's practice. RIP.

The Eagles announced "more than 45,000 fans" in attendance. Based on what I saw, I think they rounded up a bit.

For historical context, here's a look back at the team-announced attendance totals over the years:

2019 — "More than 40,000" (one practice)

2025 — "A record 60,000 fans" (one practice)

Here's the upcoming schedule (all times listed Eastern):

Wednesday, August 26 — Final training camp practice (3:00 PM start)

Thursday, August 27 — Walkthrough closed to access

Friday, August 28 — Eagles vs. Bengals (8:00 PM start)

Sunday, August 30 — 53-man roster cuts deadline at 6:00 PM

Drew Kendall logged first-team left guard reps tonight with Dickerson resting.
Tank Bigsby had a couple nice runs that looked like they would've went for big gains.

The Eagles' defense was all over designed touches to Lemon. Hurts and Lemon have also yet to totally sync up.
Lemon is in the running to be the Eagles' punt returner. He took reps in that role along with Britain Covey and Cooper DeJean .

Ramirez showed up with a TFL tonight.

No fight this time around but Moro Ojomo drove Fred Johnson multiple yards into the backfield on a rep where Barkley was stopped for just a short gain to bring up a fourth down.

For those wondering why the players were wearing jerseys with bright green numbers, it's to promote the Eagles Autism Foundation . They'll be auctioned off for charity if you want to get your hands on one.
Today I learned that former Eagles long snapper Jon Dorenbos has really long hair now.
Jolene by Dolly Parton was played on the speakers at The Linc after tonight's practice. RIP.

articles.title: Jets Receive Alarming Concerns After Practice
articles.summary: The New York Jets received some alarming concerns about the offensive line after the final training camp practice. The post Jets Receive Alarming Concerns Af...
articles.body:
The New York Jets received some alarming concerns from the final training camp practice.

Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic said on Tuesday, August 25, "By my count, the Jets backup O-Line has allowed five sacks today with Cade Klubnik at QB."

Rosenblatt wasn't the only one who noticed the shoddy play from the backups in the trenches.

"Jets backup O-line: Pass protection is leaky (understatement). Klubnik has held the ball at times but too many free rushers," ESPN's Rich Cimini posted on X.

Analyst Is Concerned With This Potential Foreshadowing

In the Week 2, 17-0 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers , the Jets allowed four sacks.

ESPN New York's Jake Asman didn't like what he saw from the backup linemen that suited up in that contest.

"Some negatives I have in my notes, and we kind of alluded to it when I talked about [Cade] Klubnik. He was under way too much pressure. The second team and third team offensive line, not very good. Now I get it, most teams probably have bad offensive lines besides their starters. The Jets last year were remarkably healthy on the offensive line. They were, we can call it for what it is. Last year, the New York Jets started the same five guys for all 17 games. Now, yes, Alijah Vera-Tucker got hurt on the Tuesday before Week 1, I get it, but they didn't have another injury to their offensive line. The odds of that happening again two years in a row feel unlikely, right?" Asman openly asked.

"I don't think they have great offensive line depth, especially in the interior … I think the backup offensive line, eh, I don't know if you can feel great about it … The Jets better hope the starting offensive line stays healthy because the depth behind it is not going to inspire a whole lot of confidence," Asman bluntly stated.

The Jets had a defensive tackle issue last season. It was abundantly clear throughout the entire offseason. Right before the start of the 2025 campaign, general manager Darren Mougey solved the problem.

He pulled off a pair of savvy trades to acquire Harrison Phillips and Jowon Briggs to fortify the position. Could Mougey make lightning strike in the same place twice?

The defensive tackle position is one of the deepest on the Jets' roster ahead of 2026, but the same can't be said for the other side of the trenches. However, the problem is that every team in the NFL doesn't have enough offensive line depth.

The supply of good linemen is always low, and the demand is always sky-high.

So if Mougey is going to pull a rabbit out of the hat, it'll be more difficult than last year. The brutally honest conversation is the Jets' depth in the trenches is going to get tested this year; it's a near guarantee.

The Jets were the only team in the NFL last year that started the same five guys on the offensive line. Gang Green hadn't accomplished that feat as an organization since 2012.

They're unlikely to pull that off in back-to-back years. That means the Jets' depth on the O-Line better be on point, or else the issues in training camp could be some serious foreshadowing for the season to come.

articles.title: Morgan Scalley just wrapped up his first fall camp as the Utes’ head coach. Here are the takeaways
articles.summary: Here's what stood out as the Utah Utes wrapped up fall camp.
articles.body:
Utah concluded fall camp on Saturday and has shifted into preparation for the season opener against Idaho on Sept. 3.

Football season is close, and Utah's players are fired up to play against someone other than their own teammates.

"I'm just excited to hit someone else other than my teammates and the people that I love around me," said linebacker Trey Reynolds. "Excited to take it out on some other people."

One of the biggest takeaways for coach Morgan Scalley is that his team got through fall camp "injury free for the most part." That hasn't always been the case at Utah, so Scalley is pleased with where the team is at as August draws to a close

"We got some bumps and bruises, guys that still need to get some rehab in, but we'll be ready to go for Game 1 and feel very good about where we're at in terms of depth chart and stuff like that — stuff I won't talk to you guys about," Scalley said.

With fall camp finished, the Utes now turn their attention to Idaho. That includes watching offensive film of Grand Valley State , where Vandals offensive coordinator Ian Shoemaker is coming from, and defensive film of Iowa State, where Idaho defensive coordinator Lee Stalker was a defensive assistant.

Idaho opens the season this Friday against Cal Poly.

"You're trying to get any sort of information you can get from where these coaches are coming from. The good news is they'll be playing on Friday, so we'll get a really good peek at that. But just making sure your guys understand how to study film the right way," Scalley said.

Utah accomplished what it needed to this fall camp, establishing the depth chart and improving tackling while staying injury-free for the most part.

One area of improvement from Utah's first scrimmage of fall camp was red zone efficiency. After the closed-to-the-media scrimmage, Scalley had this to say:

"I'd say red-zone work, kind of a mixed bag. We need to be more efficient, not enough touchdowns in the red zone, too many field goals," Scalley said.

It's safe to say that OC Kevin McGiven and the rest of the offense heard that message, as the red zone success rate was up to close camp.

"I'm glad I said that because maybe they got butthurt or something because it's been fantastic since then. So maybe they thought I was calling them out. Man, really good the next couple days. That was fantastic," Scalley said. "McGiven is a competitor, man. Maybe he heard that and was like, 'OK'. No, that was good. Yeah, we've cleaned some stuff up for sure."

As part of the march toward the start of the season, Utah announced its captains and leadership committee for 2026.

Quarterback Devon Dampier , running back Wayshawn Parker , offensive lineman Alex Harrison, linebackers Jonathan Hall and Trey Reynolds and safety Nate Ritchie were named captains.

Along with the captains, defensive ends Lance Holtzclaw and Ethan Day, safety Jackson Bennee , offensive lineman Zereoue Williams, defensive tackle Karson Kaufusi, safety Rabbit Evans, long snapper Logan Castor, tight end Noah Bennee, quarterback Byrd Ficklin , wide receivers Tobias Merriweather and Braden Pegan and linebacker Cyrus Polu were named to the team's leadership council.

"You can see it's a big one, right? You've got a big leadership council. You got a lot of guys getting a lot of votes. That's a good thing. There's not one guy in that group, whether it be from the captain group or the leadership council groups that you're going, 'Oh no.' Those guys are compelling. They're bringing others with them. It's a really solid group," Scalley said.

Here are three other takeaways as the Utes wrapped up fall camp

Utah feels like it has a very deep wide receiver room this year, with Kyri Shoels, Larry Simmons, Creed Whittemore, Ricky Johnson , Tobias Merriweather and Mana Carvalho all potentially having roles depending on the opponent and defensive matchup.

"For the first time in a long time, we've had so many good receivers to help our corners at all positions," said cornerbacks coach Sharrieff Shah.

Utah State transfer Braden Pegan, who transferred from Utah State, should be the group's WR1.

After catching 60 balls from Bryson Barnes for 926 yards and five touchdowns last season in Kevin McGiven's offense, Pegan could be a favorite target of quarterback Devon Dampier.

The 6-foot-3, 210-pound junior is one of the tallest players in the receiver room and has put that height to good use in his ability to snag 50-50 balls. While he's a big target for Dampier, he also has plenty of speed and was a threat from all over the field. He has sure hands, too, dropping just two balls on 94 targets.

If Pegan's fall camp performance is any indication, he could have a big season for the Utes.

"If Braden Pegan does what he's been doing to us, which I believe he will … It not only frustrates you, but you recognize that, all right, if we get a fifty fifty ball from him, we've done good. We've done good," said cornerbacks coach Sharieff Shah.

Utah feels confident in offensive line travel group, but still needs to decide on starting five

The good news for offensive line coach Jordan Gross is that he feels that he has 10 players that he's confident in playing in a Big 12 game.

"It's been an outstanding fall camp. All the credit goes to our players on that offensive line. Everything from no returning starters to a new offense to a new O-line coach, there's just so much that they've had to take on and every day has been just even more encouragement to me that they are all in on being a really great unit this year," Gross said.

The Utes, of course, replace all five starters from last season's fantastic offensive line, and finding the right combination of players for Utah's first game has been one of the key storylines in fall camp.

While the Utes have a great idea of who those five will be, Gross is still finalizing that starting unit.

"Honestly, still working to identify who that first five will be when we take the field. And that's a very good thing. Not, 'Oh crap, who is it going to be? Dang it, who do I need to pick out of this unit?' So been a lot of fun. I'm very lucky. It's a great group," Gross said.

Alex Harrison, Zereoue Williams, Keith Olson, Solatoa Moea'i, Kelvin Obot, Isaiah Garcia and Cedric Jefferson are expected to at least be in the rotation. Which combination of those players will start is still to be determined, and could even change after the first game if the starting group isn't playing the way they need to.

Byrd Ficklin's role will be fascinating to watch

After last season, Utah coaches are not going to let Byrd Ficklin sit idly on the sidelines. Not after directly contributing to three Ute wins and rushing for 513 yards and three touchdowns last year.

"A lot of explosiveness. A lot of explosive plays. Even when I'm on or off the field, no matter what's going to happen, something exciting is going to be on the field," Ficklin said. "Every player is going to be exciting, a lot of speed, a lot of gos, everything."

Utah has largely kept the specifics of Ficklin's offensive involvement under wraps, but he will see the field plenty this year in a variety of different positions, including some packages with Dampier at quarterback.

"I think with Byrd, it's utilization. How can you contribute and what does that look like?" McGiven said this spring. "He's like a Swiss army knife and without giving up the ship, there's a lot of different things that he can do on a play-to-play basis and different places that he can line up. And we need to be able to utilize those and get creative with those packages."

"Honestly, still working to identify who that first five will be when we take the field. And that's a very good thing. Not, 'Oh crap, who is it going to be? Dang it, who do I need to pick out of this unit?' So been a lot of fun. I'm very lucky. It's a great group," Gross said.

Alex Harrison, Zereoue Williams, Keith Olson, Solatoa Moea'i, Kelvin Obot, Isaiah Garcia and Cedric Jefferson are expected to at least be in the rotation. Which combination of those players will start is still to be determined, and could even change after the first game if the starting group isn't playing the way they need to.
Byrd Ficklin's role will be fascinating to watch

After last season, Utah coaches are not going to let Byrd Ficklin sit idly on the sidelines. Not after directly contributing to three Ute wins and rushing for 513 yards and three touchdowns last year.

"A lot of explosiveness. A lot of explosive plays. Even when I'm on or off the field, no matter what's going to happen, something exciting is going to be on the field," Ficklin said. "Every player is going to be exciting, a lot of speed, a lot of gos, everything."

Utah has largely kept the specifics of Ficklin's offensive involvement under wraps, but he will see the field plenty this year in a variety of different positions, including some packages with Dampier at quarterback.

"I think with Byrd, it's utilization. How can you contribute and what does that look like?" McGiven said this spring. "He's like a Swiss army knife and without giving up the ship, there's a lot of different things that he can do on a play-to-play basis and different places that he can line up. And we need to be able to utilize those and get creative with those packages."

articles.title: Orioles clobber Cardinals, 13-1, behind Holliday’s table-setting, Alonso’s power
articles.summary: ST. LOUIS — A few hours before the Orioles’ series opener against the Cardinals, Jackson Holliday spoke about what he expected it to feel like to play in the...
articles.body:
ST. LOUIS — A few hours before the Orioles' series opener against the Cardinals , Jackson Holliday spoke about what he expected it to feel like to play in the ballpark where he grew up watching his dad play.

The last time Holliday hit at Busch Stadium was when he was 12 years old. A decade later, Holliday said he was going to focus on putting one out during batting practice first.

"I'll try my best in BP, start there," the leadoff hitter said. "Hopefully, get a few knocks this week."

Holliday sparked the Orioles' offense to one of its most impressive outputs of the season — and the ballcub to one of its best victories of the year — by smacking three of the team's 16 hits en route to Baltimore 's 13-1 win. The offensive output is tied for the Orioles' highest this season, while their 12-run margin of victory is their best of the year.

But Holliday, whose parents and grandparents were in attendance, might not have been the happiest player on the Orioles to be in St. Louis this week. Pete Alonso , the Orioles' No. 2 hitter, entered with Ruthian numbers at Busch Stadium, and they became even more like The Great Bambino's after the Polar Bear's 4-for-4 performance.

Alonso blasted a three-run homer in the third inning and then smacked two more hits to follow Holliday in the fifth to keep the quarter in the merry-go-round of Baltimore's season-best eight-run frame. Alonso's 1.243 OPS at Busch Stadium is the best of any player with at least 75 plate appearances in the ballpark, and it's the slugger's best at any MLB stadium in which he has at least 50 plate appearances.

In total, Holliday and Alonso combined for seven hits, four runs, five RBIs and two extra-base hits.

The blowout win starts a pivotal nine-game road trip off on a much-needed high note. The Orioles (64-68) are temporarily two games back of the Cleveland Guardians for the third and final wild-card spot in the mediocre American League. Baltimore's next eight games come against a Cardinals team that's now below .500, the AL-worst Athletics and the NL-worst Rockies.

Long before the offensive outburst, the first inning had a feeling of deja vu for Baltimore's bats. Holliday reached base on an error and advanced to third on an Alonso single, but they were stranded after three straight Orioles failed to hit the ball out of the infield against Cardinals left-hander Matthew Liberatore .

Two innings later, the Orioles got runners on the corners again thanks to a Leody Taveras single and a perfectly executed hit-and-run between the outfielder and Holliday, and Alonso ensured it wouldn't go to waste by clobbering a 435-foot long ball — his 31st of the season — to left-center field. The big fly continued Alonso's scorching-hot stretch since the trade deadline, during which he's hit an eye-popping .416 with a 1.237 OPS. Christian Encarnacion-Strand , a lefty masher who's helped the Orioles improve against southpaws since he joined the team in mid-July, then put Baltimore up 4-0.

The explosion in the fifth began with the first five batters — and nine of the first 10 — reaching base. Coby Mayo hit a 107 mph line drive off shortstop JJ Wetherholt's glove for an RBI single to knock Liberatore out of the game. Encarnacion-Strand then hit a ground ball with eyes for a two-run single to put the Orioles up 7-1.

Taveras, one of the Orioles' best hitters with runners in scoring position this season, delivered with a two-run single with the bases loaded, followed by an RBI single from Holliday and an RBI double from Alonso to put the Orioles ahead 12-1. Baltimore tacked on another run in the sixth on back-to-back doubles from Christian Franklin and Dylan Beavers .

Manager Craig Albernaz then pulled Alonso, who has been managing a calf injury over the past 10 days, in the bottom of the fifth.

The victory wasn't just because of the offense, though. Chris Bassitt was steady throughout the evening to deliver 6 2/3 innings of one-run ball. The long run came on a Nathan Church solo homer in the third.

The start was perhaps Bassitt's best of the season — one that was marred by back pain and then surgery to fix it. But the 37-year-old right-hander, who was signed for $18.5 million to stabilize the rotation, has delivered three straight solid starts since returning from the injured list.

The Orioles will look to take the series Wednesday with ace Kyle Bradish on the mound opposite Cardinals right-hander Michael McGreevy .

articles.title: Is Matt Olson being overlooked in the National League MVP race?
articles.summary: Matt Olson is putting together another monster season for the Braves, and his combination of power, production and consistency has pushed him into the Nation...
articles.body:
Is Matt Olson being overlooked in the National League MVP race? originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

Matt Olson isn't the favorite to win the National League MVP award.

But dismissing the Atlanta Braves first baseman from the conversation would be increasingly difficult.

Olson has put together one of the strongest seasons of his career, entering the final stretch with 36 home runs, 77 RBIs, 31 doubles and an .865 OPS. He has accumulated 4.1 Baseball-Reference WAR while once again providing Atlanta with durability in the middle of its lineup.

He has an argument. But right now, Pete Crow-Armstrong appears to have the stronger one.

MLB.com latest MVP poll placed Crow-Armstrong atop a crowded NL race, while Shohei Ohtani remains firmly in contention despite a knee issue preventing him from pitching since July 3.

Olson's case begins with power and consistency.

On Aug. 16, Olson launched his 36th homer of the season, a three-run shot that gave Atlanta the lead against Arizona . At the time, it also gave him an MLB-leading 66 extra-base hits.

Olson finished fourth in NL MVP voting in 2023 after producing 54 home runs and 139 RBIs. Braves manager Walt Weiss believes Olson might actually be a more complete hitter now, even if he doesn't match those massive power totals.

But winning MVP requires separating from elite competition.

Crow-Armstrong has combined power, speed and premium center-field defense into perhaps the NL's best all-around season. Ohtani remains one of baseball's most dangerous offensive players, and candidates such as Kyle Schwarber are also part of the discussion.

That's where Olson faces his biggest challenge.

A first baseman must produce overwhelming offensive numbers to overcome the positional value provided by an elite defensive center fielder such as Crow-Armstrong. Olson's 4.1 bWAR is excellent, but it doesn't currently separate him from the field.

If Olson finishes with a September surge, reaches or surpasses 45 homers and helps drive Atlanta through the stretch run, voters could look at his candidacy differently.

Right now, Olson shouldn't be called the NL MVP favorite.

But he absolutely belongs in the conversation.

And with more than a month remaining, the Braves slugger still has time to turn an MVP-caliber season into an MVP-winning one.
